title: GCD: A Serial Queue Guards State
hints: A serial `DispatchQueue` runs one block at a time.
Wrap every read and write of `value` in `queue.sync`; mark the class `@unchecked Sendable`.
`func increment() { queue.sync { value += 1 } }` and `DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform(iterations: threads) { _ in … }`.
jsBridge: Before actors, a **serial `DispatchQueue`** guarded shared state: every read and write went through `queue.sync`. JS never needed this (single thread). It's the mutex pattern. `@unchecked Sendable` tells Swift 6 "trust me, I synchronise".

compass.q: Node's single thread makes counters trivially safe. What changes the moment you have two threads writing?
Serial queue vs `NSLock` vs `Mutex` (Synchronization) vs `actor`: which does 2026 Swift recommend?
Calling `queue.sync` from code already running on that queue: what happens?
Java `synchronized` blocks vs a serial queue: which one can deadlock more easily?
